DAIR.condition_interactions: Decentralized Decision-Making creates the governance architecture within which Community Capacity Building and Participatory Technology Design operate---without distributed authority, capacity building would lack channels for influence, and participatory design would lack decision-making power. Community Capacity Building provides the substrate for meaningful participation in both governance and design. Participatory Technology Design translates governance authority and community capacity into concrete technical choices.
DAIR.synthesis: DAIR demonstrates how decentralized governance, community investment, and participatory design combine to produce both internal democratic practices and external capacity-building impact. The case shows that challenging AI\'s concentrated power requires simultaneous transformation of governance structures (who decides), resource distribution (who has capacity), and design processes (how technology is shaped)---with each dimension reinforcing the others. Through the D-A-S framework, DAIR\'s design choices create affordances for distributed AI development that structure new forms of sovereignty capacity for marginalized communities.
DAIR.compact_equation: For DAIR (Distributed AI Research Institute), DD (Governance) + CCB (Resources) + PTD (Technology P) = RAWD (Dem) + SCAM (Dem) + ECCT (Imp)

Detroit CTC.condition_interactions: Community-Owned Infrastructure provides the material foundation upon which Decentralized Decision-Making can operate---governance of infrastructure requires infrastructure to govern. Capacity Building and Technological Empowerment ensures communities can exercise the authority that Decentralized Decision-Making distributes. The three conditions create a virtuous cycle: infrastructure ownership motivates capacity building, capacity building enables effective governance, and effective governance strengthens infrastructure ownership.
Detroit CTC.synthesis: Detroit CTC demonstrates how infrastructure ownership, skills development, and distributed governance combine to produce comprehensive community control over digital communications. The case shows that digital self-determination requires material foundations (owned infrastructure), human capacity (technical skills), and governance structures (distributed authority)---each necessary but insufficient alone. Detroit\'s approach creates lasting sovereignty capacity by building all three dimensions simultaneously, ensuring communities can not only access but actually control their digital infrastructure.
Detroit CTC.compact_equation: For Detroit Community Technology Project (CT, DD (Governance) + CBATE (Resources) + CI (Technology) = CCDM (Dem) + LTCE (Dem) + CDCA (Dem) + PCNE (Com) **Consolidation Notes:** > \- Merged 1 condition group(s)

DEF.condition_interactions: Bidirectional Knowledge Exchange connects local capacity building to global learning, ensuring that Democratizing Access and Skills draws on broader resources while Inclusive Participation and Representation ensures benefits reach marginalized groups. Community-Owned Infrastructure Development and Culturally-Embedded Technology Development translate these flows into tangible local assets. The conditions work as an integrated system: global connections feed local capacity, local capacity enables infrastructure development, and cultural embedding ensures relevance.
DEF.synthesis: Digital Empowerment Foundation demonstrates how global-local knowledge flows, skills democratization, and culturally-embedded infrastructure combine to produce community value and democratic practices in underserved contexts. The case shows that addressing digital divides requires not just connectivity but comprehensive capacity building that includes infrastructure, skills, cultural relevance, and governance inclusion. DEF\'s approach creates sovereignty capacity by ensuring communities have not just access to technology but the skills, culturally-appropriate tools, and governance voice to shape technology to their own purposes.
DEF.compact_equation: For Digital Empowerment Foundation, CCB (Org Info) + BKE (Partners) + CID (Technology P) + DAAS (Resources) + IPAR (Social Conte) + CTD (Technology) = CTCB (Com) + VIIW (Com) + WDAF (Com) + RKES (Bal) + ALRF (Dem) **Consolidation Notes:** > \- Merged 1 outcome group(s)

FNIGC.condition_interactions: Indigenous Knowledge Systems Integration provides the foundational orientation that shapes how all other conditions operate---without epistemological grounding, engagement with colonial institutions risks assimilation. Policy Influence and Strategic Institutional Engagement translate this grounding into external recognition, while Strategic Navigation of Regulatory Landscapes enables operation within hostile frameworks. Democratic Data Governance and Indigenous Data Sovereignty create the technical infrastructure, while Community Capacity Building ensures First Nations can actually exercise governance authority.
FNIGC.synthesis: FNIGC demonstrates how Indigenous epistemological grounding, strategic institutional engagement, and community capacity building combine to produce both policy impact and democratic data governance practices. The case shows that Indigenous data sovereignty requires simultaneous work across multiple fronts: establishing epistemological foundations, building technical infrastructure, developing community capacity, and transforming external policy frameworks---all while navigating hostile regulatory environments. FNIGC\'s success stems from holding these dimensions together, ensuring that policy victories are grounded in actual First Nations governance capacity and epistemological integrity.
FNIGC.compact_equation: For First Nations Information Governance Cen, MPATE (Governance) + SIE (Politics) + PIASC (Politics) + IKSI (Purpose) + SNORL (Regulation) + CCB (Resources) + DDG (Technology P) + IDS (Technology) = MGML (Imp) + PFRI (Imp) + RCFF (Imp) + SPAF (Dem) + FNDG (Dem) + INEP (Dem) + FNSO (Dem) **Consolidation Notes:** > \- Merged 1 outcome group(s)

GIDA.condition_interactions: Multi-Network Presence creates the infrastructure for global coordination, while Embedding in Indigenous Sovereignty Movements ensures data governance remains connected to broader self-determination struggles. Indigenous Knowledge Systems Integration provides the shared epistemological foundation that makes transnational coordination possible without bureaucratic hierarchy. Policy Influence and Self-Determined Indigenous Data Sovereignty represent complementary strategies---engaging international institutions while maintaining independence from state frameworks.
GIDA.synthesis: GIDA demonstrates how global Indigenous network coordination, epistemological grounding, and strategic policy engagement combine to produce transnational impact while maintaining Indigenous self-determination. The case shows that Indigenous data sovereignty at the global level requires building networks that amplify local efforts without creating bureaucratic hierarchies, engaging international institutions while maintaining independence from state frameworks, and grounding transnational coordination in shared Indigenous epistemologies rather than Western governance models. GIDA\'s CARE Principles represent this synthesis---principles derived from Indigenous worldviews that have achieved international institutional recognition.
GIDA.compact_equation: For Global Indigenous Data Alliance (GIDA), MP (Partners) + PIASC (Politics) + IKSI (Purpose) + SRTDS (Regulation) + EISM (Social Conte) + IDS (Technology) = TICA (Bal) + TISN (Bal) + IGFA (Imp) + GFFI (Dem) + ICAO (Dem) **Consolidation Notes:** > \- Merged 1 outcome group(s)

MAIAM NAYRI WINGARA.condition_interactions: Value Reconceptualization provides the foundational reframing that enables Democratic Data Governance to operate on different terms---without challenging the assumption that Indigenous data is public property, governance mechanisms would reproduce colonial relationships. Together, they create conditions for data governance that centers Indigenous agency and collective benefit.
MAIAM NAYRI WINGARA.synthesis: MAIAM NAYRI WINGARA demonstrates how value reconceptualization and democratic data governance combine to challenge colonial data practices and center Indigenous agency. The case shows that transforming Indigenous data governance requires not just new governance mechanisms but fundamental reconceptualization of what data is and whom it serves---shifting from data as public resource to be exploited to data as collective Indigenous asset to be governed by and for Indigenous peoples. This foundational reframing enables governance practices that genuinely center Indigenous agency rather than reproducing colonial relationships under new technical forms.
MAIAM NAYRI WINGARA.compact_equation: For MAIAM NAYRI WINGARA, VR (Purpose) + DDG (Technology P) = CVOD (Com) + AATS (Dem)

Masakhane.condition_interactions: Decolonial Technology Development provides the orienting challenge that motivates all other conditions. Inclusive Expertise Integration and Bidirectional Knowledge Exchange structure relationships between technical experts and communities in non-extractive ways. Community Capacity Building ensures benefits remain in African contexts. Culturally-Embedded Technology Development translates these relationships into technology that serves language-specific needs.
Masakhane.synthesis: Masakhane demonstrates how decolonial purpose, inclusive expertise integration, and community capacity building combine to produce both valuable technology commons and lasting African AI research capacity. The case shows that countering Western AI dominance requires not just creating African language technology but fundamentally restructuring how AI research is conducted---building non-extractive relationships between technical experts and linguistic communities, ensuring community ownership of outputs, and developing capacity for ongoing African-led research. Masakhane\'s distributed, community-driven model creates sovereignty capacity that persists beyond any single project.
Masakhane.compact_equation: For Masakhane, IEI (Partners) + BKE (Partners) + VRA (Resources) + CCB (Resources) + DTD (Problem) + CSAKP (Purpose) + CTD (Technology P) = PIOT (Dem) + ODAT (Com) + CATW (Com) + UPEL (Bal) + ALTC (Imp) + ALNC (Imp) **Consolidation Notes:** > \- Merged 1 outcome group(s)

Monlam AI.condition_interactions: Cultural Heritage Preservation through Technology provides urgency---the threat of cultural erasure motivates action. Cultural Sovereignty and Knowledge Preservation orients that action toward sovereignty rather than mere preservation. Community-Controlled Technology Development ensures external partnerships serve rather than compromise community control. Culturally-Embedded Technology Development translates these orientations into technology that embodies Buddhist scholarly traditions.
Monlam AI.synthesis: Monlam AI demonstrates how cultural threat response, sovereignty-oriented purpose, and community-controlled partnerships combine to produce technology that serves Tibetan cultural preservation under conditions of political suppression. The case shows that cultural and linguistic sovereignty in threatened contexts requires technology that does more than digitize heritage---it must be controlled by community institutions, developed according to cultural protocols, and oriented toward sovereignty rather than mere preservation. Monlam\'s integration with monastic institutions ensures that technology serves cultural continuity as defined by Tibetan traditions themselves.
Monlam AI.compact_equation: For Monlam AI, CTD (Partners) + CHPTT (Problem) + CSAKP (Purpose) + CTD (Technology) = TDAW (Bal) + TLST (Imp) + TLTP (Imp) + TNTI (Com)

Te Hiku Media.condition_interactions: Alternative Value Definition reframes what counts as success, enabling rejection of extractive partnerships. Indigenous Knowledge Systems Integration and Cultural Sovereignty provide the orientation that shapes technology development. Legal Innovation for Community Control creates protective frameworks. Indigenous Data Sovereignty structures external relationships. Culturally-Embedded Technology Development translates these into world-leading technology that serves Māori purposes.
Te Hiku Media.synthesis: Te Hiku Media demonstrates how Indigenous epistemological grounding, protective legal innovation, and culturally-embedded technology development combine to produce world-leading language technology under full community control. The case shows that Indigenous technology sovereignty requires not just building good technology but fundamentally restructuring ownership, governance, and purpose---rejecting extractive partnerships, creating novel legal protections, grounding development in Indigenous knowledge systems, and redefining value beyond narrow economic metrics. Te Hiku\'s Kaitiakitanga License represents a breakthrough in legal innovation that other Indigenous communities are now adopting.
Te Hiku Media.compact_equation: For Te Hiku Media, IDS (Partners) + AVD (Problem) + IKSI (Purpose) + CSAKP (Purpose) + LIFCC (Regulation) + CTD (Technology) = ITDR (Bal) + CSAL (Com) + HMLT (Com) + MCGE (Dem) + LFPM (Dem) + WMLA (Imp)

Te Mana Raraunga.condition_interactions: Indigenous Knowledge Systems Integration provides the epistemological foundation that shapes all other work. Decolonial Research Ethics identifies what needs to change in existing frameworks. Multi-Network Presence connects local efforts to global movements, amplifying voice. Policy Influence and Systemic Change translates these into formal institutional recognition.
Te Mana Raraunga.synthesis: Te Mana Raraunga demonstrates how Indigenous epistemological grounding, network coordination, and strategic policy engagement combine to produce formal institutional recognition of Māori data sovereignty. The case shows that transforming national data governance requires both conceptual work (establishing what Indigenous data sovereignty means in Māori terms) and strategic engagement (building networks, engaging institutions, securing formal agreements). The Mana Ōrite Agreement with Stats NZ represents a significant achievement in translating Indigenous data sovereignty principles into governmental practice.
Te Mana Raraunga.compact_equation: For Te Mana Raraunga, MP (Partners) + PIASC (Politics) + DRE (Problem) + IKSI (Purpose) = TICA (Bal) + FARM (Imp) + CGGR (Dem) + MDGA (Dem)

TIC A.C..condition_interactions: Resistance and Construction Integration provides the strategic orientation---combining opposition with building. Strategic Regulatory Navigation translates this into concrete regulatory victories. Community-Owned Infrastructure provides the material foundation that both motivates regulatory engagement and benefits from regulatory victories. Prioritizing Local Needs ensures that both regulatory strategy and infrastructure development serve community purposes.
TIC A.C..synthesis: TIC A.C. demonstrates how resistance-construction integration, strategic regulatory navigation, and community infrastructure ownership combine to produce indigenous telecommunications autonomy in hostile regulatory environments. The case shows that community telecommunications in contexts of regulatory hostility requires simultaneous work on multiple fronts: building actual infrastructure that serves communities, engaging regulatory systems strategically to secure operating space, and maintaining community governance over both infrastructure and regulatory engagement. TIC A.C.\'s victory---overturning \$50,000 annual spectrum fees---represents a breakthrough that creates space for other community networks across Mexico.
TIC A.C..compact_equation: For Telecomunicaciones Indígenas Comunitaria, RACI (Purpose) + PLNIGE (Purpose) + SRN (Regulation) + CI (Technology) = LVEI (Dem) + CADT (Bal) + REES (Imp) **Consolidation Notes:** > \- Merged 1 outcome group(s)

WAO.condition_interactions: Worker-Led Transparency Mechanisms and Algorithmic Accountability and Transparency work together to expose what platforms hide. Democratic Data Governance ensures workers control the data they generate through this exposure. Inclusive Expertise Integration enables productive collaboration between workers and researchers. Resistance and Construction Integration ensures that exposure leads to both advocacy and tool-building.
WAO.synthesis: WAO demonstrates how worker-led transparency, hybrid expertise integration, and resistance-construction integration combine to produce tools that expose platform algorithmic manipulation while building worker capacity for ongoing advocacy. The case shows that algorithmic accountability requires not just technical analysis but worker-controlled investigation processes that generate evidence workers can use for advocacy. WAO\'s approach creates ongoing capacity for workers to document, understand, and challenge algorithmic management---addressing the fundamental information asymmetry that enables platform exploitation.
WAO.compact_equation: For Worker Algorithm Observatory (WAO), IEI (Governance) + WTM (Problem) + RACI (Purpose) + DDG (Technology P) + AAAT (Technology) = HGCD (Com) + WTEA (Dem) + WDEA (Dem) + WAIT (Dem) **Consolidation Notes:** > \- Merged 1 outcome group(s)

ARDC.condition_interactions: Technology Design for Multi-Scale Governance creates infrastructure that enables Bidirectional Knowledge Exchange at national scale. Ethical Data Governance Frameworks ensures that exchange operates within appropriate protections. Public-Community Co-Investment Models provides the sustainable resourcing that enables ongoing operation.
ARDC.synthesis: ARDC demonstrates how multi-scale infrastructure design, ethical governance frameworks, and diversified resourcing combine to produce national research data commons that balance openness with protection. The case shows that research data infrastructure requires deliberate design for multiple scales---supporting both institutional autonomy and national coordination---combined with governance frameworks that navigate tensions between openness and protection, and sustainable funding models that prevent dependence on single sources. ARDC\'s federated approach creates infrastructure that serves varied research contexts while maintaining coherence.
ARDC.compact_equation: For Australian Research Data Commons, BKE (Partners) + TDFMG (Technology P) + EDGF (Regulation) + PCM (Resources) = NRDI (Bal) + MRDG (Bal) + CSDA (Bal) + DFEL (Com)

Guifi.net.condition_interactions: Community-Owned Infrastructure Development provides the motivating problem. Multi-Scalar Federated Governance and Federated Governance Models work together---technical architecture and governance structure designed for federation. Legal Innovation secures the framework. Economic Transformation ensures value stays local. Decentralized Decision-Making and Community-Controlled Economic Circulation operationalize these at local levels.
Guifi.net.synthesis: Guifi.net demonstrates how federated governance design, legal innovation, and community ownership combine to produce one of the world\'s largest community-owned telecommunications networks. The case shows that community infrastructure at scale requires deliberate federation---technical architecture and governance structures designed to enable both local autonomy and network coordination---combined with legal innovation that protects community ownership and economic design that keeps value local. Guifi.net\'s recognition as a public utility commons represents a legal breakthrough that secures community infrastructure against privatization.
Guifi.net.compact_equation: For Guifi.net, FGM (Governance) + DD (Org Info) + CEC (Org Info+C57) + CID (Problem) + LIFCC (Regulation) + ETAVR (Resources) + MFG (Technology P) + CI (Technology) = FSCL (Bal) + BFEB (Bal) + LCCO (Dem) + LPMC (Dem) + CCTS (Dem) + LCCO (Imp) + CVTL (Imp) + NCT (Com)

Linux Foundation.condition_interactions: Open Source Commons Development provides the orienting problem. Open-Source Development and Open Access and Transparency create the technical commons. Open Source Community Development structures how corporate sponsors and community contributors interact. Economic Transformation ensures organizational sustainability without compromising community control.
Linux Foundation.synthesis: Linux Foundation demonstrates how open source governance, diversified resourcing, and transparent development combine to produce essential software infrastructure that remains accessible while engaging corporate resources. The case shows that sustaining critical software commons requires navigating tensions between corporate engagement and community control---creating governance structures that leverage corporate resources without compromising openness, diversifying funding to maintain independence, and maintaining transparent processes that enable community scrutiny. The result is foundational software infrastructure that serves as genuine public utility.
Linux Foundation.compact_equation: For Linux Foundation, OSCD (Partners) + ET (Resources) + OSCD (Problem) + OAAT (Technology P) + OD (Technology P) = BELC (Bal) + DRSM (Com) + CGEP (Com) + OCDW (Dem) + ESRA (Dem)

Matrix.condition_interactions: Technological Sovereignty Architecture defines the problem: enabling local control without sacrificing interoperability. Federated Governance Models and Technology Design for Multi-Scale Governance address this through both governance structure and technical design. Open Standards Development and Open-Source Development create the protocols and software as commons. Policy Influence engages external systems on behalf of open approaches.
Matrix.synthesis: Matrix demonstrates how federated design, open standards development, and policy engagement combine to produce communication infrastructure that resolves the tension between local sovereignty and global interoperability. The case shows that building genuinely decentralized communications requires technical architecture designed for federation, governance structures that enable local control, open protocols that prevent proprietary lock-in, and policy engagement that shapes broader communications standards. Matrix\'s growing adoption by governments and institutions demonstrates that federated, open approaches can compete with centralized platforms.
Matrix.compact_equation: For Matrix, FGM (Governance) + OSD (Org Info) + PIASC (Politics) + TSA (Problem) + OD (Technology P) + TDFMG (Technology P) = FACL (Bal) + MTAA (Bal) + CCOC (Dem) + USOP (Dem) + OPSI (Imp) + OPEC (Com)

Nea Guinea/Tzoumakers.condition_interactions: Decentralized Decision-Making creates the governance context within which Culturally-Embedded Technology Development can operate---community members have authority to shape what gets made and how. Together, they enable participatory design that draws on local knowledge.
Nea Guinea/Tzoumakers.synthesis: Nea Guinea/Tzoumakers demonstrates how decentralized governance and culturally-embedded technology development combine to produce a participatory maker space that bridges traditional agricultural knowledge with modern fabrication. The case shows that community-led technology development in traditional contexts requires governance structures that distribute decision-making authority and design processes that genuinely integrate local knowledge rather than imposing external solutions. The result is technology that serves local needs while building on cultural heritage.
Nea Guinea/Tzoumakers.compact_equation: For Nea Guinea/Tzoumakers, DD (Governance) + CTD (Technology) = PMSE (Dem) + DTIT (Bal)

OpenAgriNet.condition_interactions: Technology Design for Multi-Scale Governance addresses the technical challenge of serving smallholder farmers while maintaining global interoperability. Decentralized Technological Architecture ensures that farmer governance isn\'t subordinated to state or corporate frameworks.
OpenAgriNet.synthesis: OpenAgriNet demonstrates how decentralized architecture and multi-scale design combine to produce agricultural data infrastructure that serves smallholder farmers while maintaining global connectivity. The case shows that agricultural technology serving small farmers requires deliberate design for their governance needs---not scaling down corporate solutions but building from farmer requirements up---while maintaining interoperability that enables participation in broader markets and knowledge networks.
OpenAgriNet.compact_equation: For OpenAgriNet, DTA (Regulation) + TDFMG (Technology P) = OAIS (Bal) + FATW (Bal)

OpenStreetMap.condition_interactions: Global-Local Network Formation structures how global standards and local mapping practices interact. Commons-Based Resource Governance and Open Access and Transparency govern the shared resource. Digital Resources as Commons and Open Source Commons Development create and maintain the mapping data as commons.
OpenStreetMap.synthesis: OpenStreetMap demonstrates how global-local network formation, commons governance, and open access combine to produce the world\'s most comprehensive open geographic database. The case shows that global commons require deliberate navigation between universal standards and local specificity---creating governance that enables both consistency and adaptation, technical infrastructure that supports diverse contributors, and access frameworks that ensure universal availability. OSM\'s success demonstrates that volunteer-driven commons can compete with and exceed corporate alternatives.
OpenStreetMap.compact_equation: For OpenStreetMap, GNF (Social Conte) + CRG (Technology P) + OAAT (Technology P) + DRAC (Technology) + OSCD (Technology) = LMAW (Bal) + SPWC (Bal) + OMCA (Dem) + VOEM (Dem) + FGDE (Com)

P2P Foundation.condition_interactions: Commons-Based Knowledge Production orients all other work. Multi-Network Presence and Bidirectional Knowledge Exchange create infrastructure for knowledge circulation. Policy Influence and Systemic Change translates commons advocacy into policy discourse. Digital Resources as Commons creates the practical outputs.
P2P Foundation.synthesis: P2P Foundation demonstrates how commons-oriented knowledge production, multi-network positioning, and policy engagement combine to produce both practical knowledge resources and growing policy influence for commons-based approaches. The case shows that advancing the commons paradigm requires comprehensive infrastructure---documentation of existing commons initiatives, conceptual frameworks for understanding them, network connections across the movement, and policy engagement that introduces commons into mainstream discourse. P2P Foundation\'s work has helped establish commons as a recognized policy paradigm.
P2P Foundation.compact_equation: For P2P Foundation, CKP (Org Info) + BKE (Partners) + MP (Partners) + PIASC (Politics) + DRAC (Technology) = CGMD (Com) + CCES (Com) + RKFB (Bal) + TKIS (Bal) + CFEP (Imp)

RDA.condition_interactions: Bidirectional Knowledge Exchange creates the social infrastructure for data sharing. Open Standards Development creates the technical standards that enable sharing across diverse research contexts.
RDA.synthesis: Research Data Alliance demonstrates how bidirectional exchange and flexible standards development combine to produce global research data sharing infrastructure. The case shows that research data commons require both social infrastructure (relationships and agreements across institutions and disciplines) and technical standards (interoperability frameworks)---with the key insight that standards must be flexible enough to accommodate disciplinary diversity rather than imposing uniformity.

Sensorica.condition_interactions: Stigmergic Coordination Systems enables coordination at scale without hierarchy---participants contribute based on signals rather than direction. Multi-Sector Innovation Networks brings diverse actors into this coordination. Alternative Economic Models experiments with how to distribute value in open networks. Open-Source Development ensures outputs remain commons.
Sensorica.synthesis: Sensorica demonstrates how stigmergic coordination, multi-sector networks, and alternative economic experimentation combine to produce a novel model for open hardware development and commons-based peer production. The case shows that enabling distributed innovation at scale requires coordination mechanisms beyond both hierarchy and market---stigmergic systems that enable contribution based on signals rather than direction, combined with value accounting systems that can fairly distribute rewards across distributed contributors. Sensorica\'s open value network model represents an important experiment in post-capitalist economic organization.
Sensorica.compact_equation: For Sensorica, SCS (Governance) + MIN (Partners) + AEM (Resources) + OD (Technology P) = DDWT (Dem) + RRCT (Bal) + NOSE (Com) + OCRE (Com)

Solar Commons.condition_interactions: Community Asset Development Through Legal Innovation provides the orienting purpose---framing solar as community wealth opportunity. Legal Innovation for Community Control creates the trust structures that make this possible. Economic Transformation and Value Redistribution operationalizes value retention.
Solar Commons.synthesis: Solar Commons demonstrates how purposeful community asset development, legal innovation, and value redistribution combine to produce solar infrastructure that generates lasting community wealth rather than extractive investor returns. The case shows that community benefit from renewable energy requires deliberate legal and economic design---not just installing solar panels but structuring ownership, governance, and value flows so that benefits accrue to communities long-term. Solar Commons\' trust model represents an innovation that other communities are now adapting.
Solar Commons.compact_equation: For Solar Commons, CADTLI (Purpose) + LIFCC (Regulation) + ETAVR (Resources) = IFCE (Com) + SBGL (Com) + CTHS (Dem)

WikiHouse.condition_interactions: Open Source Manufacturing Networks provides the organizational model. Open-Source Development creates the designs as commons. Digital Resources as Commons ensures practical accessibility.
WikiHouse.synthesis: WikiHouse demonstrates how open source organizational models and commons-based production combine to produce housing designs that democratize construction knowledge. The case shows that extending open source principles to physical production requires not just releasing designs but creating infrastructure for distributed fabrication---design systems that enable local adaptation and production, documentation that supports non-expert builders, and licensing that prevents enclosure. WikiHouse represents an important experiment in extending digital commons principles to the built environment.
WikiHouse.compact_equation: For WikiHouse, OSMN (Org Info) + OD (Technology P) + DRAC (Technology) = OCEL (Com) + FAHD (Com) + HKCA (Com)

CoopCycle.condition_interactions: Worker Ownership Structures provides the foundational alternative to gig platforms. Federated Scaling Strategy and Scale and Democratic Participation Navigation address how to grow while maintaining democratic character. Legal Innovation for Community Control protects cooperative technology from corporate capture. Value Redistribution Mechanisms operationalizes the economic alternative.
CoopCycle.synthesis: CoopCycle demonstrates how worker ownership, federated governance, and legal innovation combine to produce a transnational delivery platform that retains value for workers while maintaining democratic governance at scale. The case shows that platform cooperativism requires addressing multiple dimensions simultaneously: ownership structures that anchor worker control, federation strategies that enable growth without sacrificing local autonomy, and legal innovations that prevent corporate appropriation of cooperative technology. CoopCycle\'s Coopyleft license represents an important innovation for protecting cooperative technology commons.
CoopCycle.compact_equation: For CoopCycle, WOS (Governance) + SADPN (Governance) + FSS (Governance) + LIFCC (Regulation) + VRM (Resources) = WATE (Com) + WVTC (Com) + FSBE (Dem) + LPET (Dem) + TGWL (Imp)

Fairbnb.coop.condition_interactions: Anti-Extractive Value Distribution provides the foundational orientation. Community-Controlled Technology Development ensures technology choices serve cooperative values. Economic Transformation and Value Redistribution operationalizes community benefit.
Fairbnb.coop.synthesis: Fairbnb.coop demonstrates how anti-extractive organizational design, community-controlled development, and value redistribution combine to produce a vacation rental platform that benefits rather than harms host communities. The case shows that platform cooperativism in the sharing economy requires fundamental redesign of value flows---not just worker ownership but community benefit structures that address the externalities (housing displacement, over-tourism) that extractive platforms create.
Fairbnb.coop.compact_equation: For Fairbnb.coop, AVD (Org Info) + CSWGN (Partners) + VRM (Resources) = CPFT (Com) + TRRT (Com) + LGMC (Bal)

Groupmuse.condition_interactions: Value Reconceptualization provides the foundational reframing---music events as community value creation rather than commercial transaction. Community Ownership for Wealth Retention structures ownership to retain that value.
Groupmuse.synthesis: Groupmuse demonstrates how cooperative ownership and value reconceptualization combine to produce a platform for house concerts that retains cultural value within communities rather than extracting it. The case shows that cooperative alternatives in cultural sectors require not just ownership restructuring but fundamental reframing of what counts as value---centering cultural and social benefit rather than profit metrics.
Groupmuse.compact_equation: For Groupmuse, COFWR (Governance) + VR (Purpose) = CSRC (Com) + CMEC (Com)

Les Mercedes.condition_interactions: Feminist Economic Transformation provides the distinctive orientation---addressing patriarchal exclusion in urban mobility work. Prioritizing Local Needs ensures alternatives serve specific neighborhood contexts. Alternative Economic Models enables experimentation with cooperative forms.
Les Mercedes.synthesis: Les Mercedes demonstrates how feminist economic orientation, local grounding, and cooperative experimentation combine to produce delivery work alternatives that center gender equity and neighborhood needs. The case shows that platform cooperativism can address multiple dimensions of exclusion simultaneously---not just worker exploitation but gendered exclusion from urban mobility work---while remaining grounded in specific local contexts rather than scaling generic solutions.
Les Mercedes.compact_equation: For Les Mercedes, FET (Purpose) + PLNIGE (Org Info) + AEM (Resources) = IEOW (Dem) + LAAS (Bal) + CSPF (Com)

Loomio.condition_interactions: Collective Ownership and Governance and Decentralized Decision-Making together structure internal democratic practice. Open-Source Development ensures the tools themselves are commons. Transparent and Participatory Design creates technology that enables deliberation across barriers.
Loomio.synthesis: Loomio demonstrates how worker cooperative governance, open source development, and participatory design combine to produce both a democratically-governed organization and tools that enable democratic deliberation in other organizations. The case shows that creating technology for democracy requires practicing democracy---Loomio\'s internal cooperative governance informs the design of tools that enable deliberation, creating a feedback loop between organizational practice and technology development.
Loomio.compact_equation: For Loomio, DD (Governance) + COAG (Org Info) + OD (Technology P) + TAPD (Technology) = NCGW (Dem) + RCRW (Dem) + APEI (Dem) + FAOT (Com)

MiData.condition_interactions: Cooperative Data Stewardship and Community Ownership for Wealth Retention together anchor data governance in member control. Federated Democratic Governance enables coordination across cooperatives. Democratic Data Governance provides the technical mechanisms for consent and governance.
MiData.synthesis: MiData demonstrates how cooperative ownership, federated governance, and democratic data practices combine to produce health data infrastructure that enables beneficial research while maintaining individual and collective control. The case shows that data cooperativism requires not just ownership restructuring but governance design that enables both individual consent and collective decision-making, combined with federation that enables coordination across contexts without sacrificing local sovereignty.
MiData.compact_equation: For MiData, COFWR (Governance) + FDG (Governance) + CDS (Org Info) + DDG (Technology P) = CDGR (Com) + CHDS (Dem) + ICEC (Bal) **Consolidation Notes:** > \- Merged 1 outcome group(s)

Namma Yatri.condition_interactions: Worker-Owned Platform Alternative (Org Info) establishes the ownership foundation. Worker-Owned Platform Alternative (Politics) navigates the strategic challenge of market engagement. Economic Transformation operationalizes zero-commission model.
Namma Yatri.synthesis: Namma Yatri demonstrates how worker ownership and economic transformation combine to produce a zero-commission ride-hailing platform that proves non-extractive models can compete in the market. The case shows that platform cooperativism can directly challenge extractive platforms by eliminating the commission that enables extraction---creating proof of concept that worker-owned alternatives are economically viable while dramatically improving worker earnings.
Namma Yatri.compact_equation: For Namma Yatri, WPA (Org Info) + WPA (Politics) + ETAVR (Resources) = WOWF (Com) + MADV (Imp) + ZMMD (Imp)

SOLshare.condition_interactions: Climate Crisis Response provides urgency and orientation. Technology Design for Multi-Scale Governance and Decentralized Technological Architecture together create the technical architecture for peer-to-peer trading. Community-Owned Infrastructure ensures communities own the resulting systems.
SOLshare.synthesis: SOLshare demonstrates how climate crisis response, multi-scale architecture, and decentralized technology combine to produce peer-to-peer energy trading that maximizes solar utilization while building community climate resilience. The case shows that community energy innovation requires technical architecture designed for peer-to-peer trading within broader grid contexts---not off-grid isolation but integration that maintains community control while enabling efficient resource sharing.
SOLshare.compact_equation: For SOLshare, CCR (Social Conte) + TDFMG (Technology P) + CI (Technology) + DTA (Technology) = CESP (Imp) + MEIE (Bal) + CESI (Dem) + RPET (Com)

Som Energia.condition_interactions: Community Ownership for Wealth Retention structures economic benefit retention. Community Resilience and Ecological Sustainability ensures economic transformation serves broader ecological and social purposes.
Som Energia.synthesis: Som Energia demonstrates how cooperative ownership and ecological purpose combine to produce renewable energy infrastructure that keeps benefits within member communities while advancing broader energy transition. The case shows that community energy cooperatives can achieve scale---Som Energia has over 70,000 members---while maintaining democratic governance and ecological orientation.
Som Energia.compact_equation: For Som Energia, COFWR (Governance) + CRAES (Purpose) = CREK (Com) + IMCE (Imp)

The Drivers Cooperative.condition_interactions: Worker Ownership Structures and Collective Ownership and Governance together anchor driver control. Economic Transformation operationalizes value retention. Policy Influence and Systemic Change translates cooperative success into policy advocacy. Transparent and Participatory Design navigates tensions between transparency and privacy.
The Drivers Cooperative.synthesis: The Drivers Cooperative demonstrates how worker ownership, democratic governance, and economic transformation combine to produce a driver-owned ride-hailing platform that proves cooperative alternatives can succeed in competitive markets. The case shows that platform cooperativism requires simultaneous work on ownership, governance, economics, and policy---creating alternatives that demonstrate viability while advocating for regulatory frameworks that support worker ownership. TDC\'s success in increasing driver earnings by 8-10% provides concrete evidence for policy engagement.
The Drivers Cooperative.compact_equation: For The Drivers Cooperative, WOS (Governance) + COAG (Governance) + PIASC (Politics) + ETAVR (Resources) + TAPD (Technology P) = DEM (Com) + DGWT (Dem) + MTAR (Dem) + WPMI (Imp) + TWPW (Imp)

Zenzeleni.condition_interactions: Community-Owned Infrastructure provides the material foundation. Capacity Building and Technological Empowerment ensures communities can maintain what they own. Community Revenue Retention structures economic benefit retention.
Zenzeleni.synthesis: Zenzeleni demonstrates how community infrastructure ownership, local capacity building, and revenue retention combine to produce telecommunications that serves rural South African communities while keeping economic benefits local. The case shows that community telecommunications requires not just infrastructure but the capacity to maintain it---building local technical skills alongside physical networks---combined with economic structures that prevent external value extraction.
Zenzeleni.compact_equation: For Zenzeleni, CRR (Org Info) + CBATE (Resources) + CI (Technology) = LECA (Com) + LTCF (Dem) + CTSR (Dem)

CLEAR.condition_interactions: Decolonial Research Ethics restructures knowledge relationships as the foundation. Democratizing Access and Skills enables community participation in research. Inclusive Participation and Representation ensures marginalized voices are centered. Resistance and Construction Integration maintains strategic orientation. Policy Influence translates research into policy change.
CLEAR.synthesis: CLEAR demonstrates how decolonial research ethics, equipment democratization, and inclusive participation combine to produce community science that generates both knowledge and policy change while centering marginalized perspectives. The case shows that decolonizing research requires not just acknowledging community knowledge but restructuring research relationships so communities control the process---combined with practical democratization of research tools and deliberate inclusion of marginalized voices in knowledge production.
CLEAR.compact_equation: For CLEAR (Civic Laboratory for Environmenta, DRE (Partners) + RACI (Politics) + PIASC (Politics) + DAAS (Resources) + IPAR (Social Conte) = CCOR (Imp) + CSIP (Imp) + IABA (Dem) + CPCM (Dem) + ARTD (Com)

DECODE.condition_interactions: Bidirectional Knowledge Exchange creates the partnership ecosystem. Democratic Data Governance provides the governance mechanisms. Open-Source Development ensures tools are available as commons for other cities.
DECODE.synthesis: DECODE demonstrates how multi-partner exchange, democratic data governance, and open source development combine to produce citizen-controlled data infrastructure integrated with municipal democracy. The case shows that municipal data sovereignty requires both technical tools and governance mechanisms---creating the technical infrastructure for citizen data control while integrating with existing democratic institutions---with open source development ensuring tools can be adopted by other cities.
DECODE.compact_equation: For DECODE, BKE (Partners) + DDG (Technology P) + OD (Technology P) = MEEC (Bal) + CDGI (Dem) + ODST (Com)

Enspiral.condition_interactions: Decentralized Decision-Making creates governance structures for distributed authority. Multi-Network Presence connects enterprises. Alternative Economic Models enables economic experimentation through participatory budgeting.
Enspiral.synthesis: Enspiral demonstrates how decentralized governance, network coordination, and participatory economics combine to produce a collaborative network of social enterprises that amplify each other\'s impact. The case shows that supporting social enterprise requires moving beyond isolated organizations to networked forms---creating governance structures for distributed decision-making, connection infrastructure for mutual support, and economic mechanisms for participatory resource allocation.
Enspiral.compact_equation: For Enspiral, DD (Governance) + MP (Partners) + AEM (Resources) = SCSD (Dem) + CNAS (Bal) + PRAA (Com)

Open Mobility Foundation.condition_interactions: Municipal/Public Digital Governance provides the foundational positioning. Multi-Network Presence and Technology Design for Multi-Scale Governance create infrastructure for city coordination. Policy Influence and Strategic Regulatory Navigation engage external systems. Transparent and Participatory Design ensures accountability.
Open Mobility Foundation.synthesis: Open Mobility Foundation demonstrates how municipal positioning, city network coordination, and policy engagement combine to produce public infrastructure for city control over mobility data. The case shows that municipal data sovereignty requires collective action---individual cities lack leverage against global mobility platforms, but networks of cities can establish standards, share development costs, and advocate collectively for regulatory frameworks that recognize municipal data authority.
Open Mobility Foundation.compact_equation: For Open Mobility Foundation, MDIG (Org Info) + MP (Partners) + PIASC (Politics) + SRN (Regulation) + TAPD (Technology) + TDFMG (Technology P) = CMDS (Bal) + NOCC (Bal) + CMGW (Bal) + RFRD (Imp) + PTDW (Dem) **Consolidation Notes:** > \- Merged 1 outcome group(s)

OpenSAFELY.condition_interactions: Privacy-Preserving Technology Design and Ethical Data Governance Frameworks together structure the balance between access and protection. Democratic Data Governance creates transparent mechanisms. Bidirectional Knowledge Exchange enables productive research partnerships.
OpenSAFELY.synthesis: OpenSAFELY demonstrates how privacy-preserving design, ethical governance, and transparent data practices combine to produce health data research infrastructure that enables beneficial research while maintaining public accountability. The case shows that privacy-preserving research requires not just technical solutions but ethical frameworks and governance mechanisms---creating comprehensive infrastructure that makes the case for transparency against assumptions that health research requires opacity.
OpenSAFELY.compact_equation: For OpenSAFELY, PTD (Partners) + EDGF (Regulation) + BKE (Resources) + DDG (Technology P) = TPRW (Imp) + CPSW (Bal) + PBIS (Bal) + PRAM (Dem)

Participatory Brazil.condition_interactions: Democratization of Governance and Technology and Decentralized Decision-Making create the governance framework. Transparent and Participatory Design provides the technical platform. Community Capacity Building ensures citizens can participate effectively. Inclusive Participation and Representation extends reach. Purpose as Civic Obligation provides motivational framing.
Participatory Brazil.synthesis: Participatory Brazil demonstrates how digital platforms, capacity building, and inclusive design combine to produce government infrastructure for citizen participation in policy-making. The case shows that digital participatory governance requires comprehensive infrastructure---not just platforms but capacity building for effective participation, inclusion mechanisms for marginalized citizens, and cultural framing that positions participation as civic responsibility. The integration of digital and deliberative elements addresses limitations of purely online engagement.
Participatory Brazil.compact_equation: For Participatory Brazil, DOGAT (Governance) + DD (Governance) + TAPD (Technology) + HDPA (Org Info) + CCB (Resources) + PACO (Purpose) + IPAR (Social Conte) = GPEC (Imp) + ECCF (Imp) + OCPE (Dem) + PPDD (Dem) + DIEC (Dem) + CCOG (Dem) + DPDW (Dem)

SDI.condition_interactions: Multi-Network Presence creates the transnational infrastructure. Democratization of Governance and Technology and Community Capacity Building enable resident-led data practices. Prioritizing Local Needs ensures global engagement serves local priorities. Climate Justice Integration connects housing and climate agendas.
SDI.synthesis: Slum Dwellers International demonstrates how resident-led data practices, transnational networking, and climate justice integration combine to produce community-led urban development recognized by governments globally. The case shows that transforming urban governance requires community capacity for data generation and advocacy, transnational networks for solidarity and amplification, and framing that connects housing justice with climate adaptation---ensuring global engagement serves local priorities rather than imposing external agendas.
SDI.compact_equation: For Slum Dwellers International, DOGAT (Governance) + PLNIGE (Org Info) + MP (Partners) + CCB (Resources) + CJI (Social Conte) = RUDR (Imp) + CDEL (Imp) + CCAI (Imp) + CDWT (Bal) + TNAC (Bal)

Stop LAPD Spying Coalition.condition_interactions: Inclusive Participation and Representation ensures affected community leadership---foundational for legitimacy. Community Capacity Building and Algorithmic Accountability and Transparency together enable documentation and exposure. Resistance and Construction Integration provides strategic orientation. Policy Influence translates into concrete victories.
Stop LAPD Spying Coalition.synthesis: Stop LAPD Spying Coalition demonstrates how affected community leadership, capacity building, surveillance mapping, and strategic policy engagement combine to produce concrete victories against police surveillance systems. The case shows that effective accountability movements require affected community leadership for legitimacy, capacity building for sustained engagement, technical tools for documenting surveillance systems, and strategic policy engagement that translates exposure into elimination. The shutdown of LAPD\'s predictive policing programs represents a model for anti-surveillance movements nationally.
Stop LAPD Spying Coalition.compact_equation: For Stop LAPD Spying Coalition, RACI (Politics) + PIASC (Politics) + CCB (Resources) + AAAT (Technology) + IPAR (Social Conte) = SOLO (Dem) + SMES (Dem) + DCLI (Dem) + PVES (Imp) + CCTD (Imp)
